chunks: Muhammad ibn Isma'il, from al-Fadl ibn Shazaan, from Safwan ibn Yahya, from Muawiya ibn 'Ammar, from Abu 'Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The performer of the 'Umra, when he ushers the sacrificial animal, shaves (his head) before he slaughters (it).

key_terms.الْهَدْيَ: The sacrificial animal brought by the pilgrim

ai.seo_question: When should a pilgrim shave their head during Umra if they have brought a sacrificial animal?
ai.summary: This hadith from al-Kafi clarifies the procedural sequence of rites for a Mufrid (one performing Umra alone) who brings a hady, establishing that head shaving (halq) must precede the slaughter of the sacrificial animal. This ruling is significant in Shia jurisprudence as it distinguishes the specific order of obligations for Umra from the combined Hajj and Umra (Qiran) or Hajj only (Tamattu'), ensuring the pilgrim exits the state of Ihram correctly after fulfilling the sacrifice. The emphasis on sequence highlights the precision required in ritual acts to ensure the validity of the pilgrimage.

en.hubeali:
Muhammad Bin Ismail, from Al Fazl Bin Shazaan, from Safwan Bin Yahya, from Muawiya Bin Ammar, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The performer of the Umra, when he ushers the sacrificial animal, would shave off (his head) before he slaughters’.
en.sarwar: 4. Muhammad ibn ‘Isma’il has narrated from al-Fadl ibn Shadhan from Safwan ibn Yahya from Mu‘awiyah ibn ‘Ammar who has said the following: “Abu ‘Abd Allah, ‘Alayhi al-Salam, has said, ‘
One who drives an animal for offering in al-‘Umrah without al-Hajj must slaughter it before shaving.’”
